thought_title: Born and unborn, God in man

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Εἰώθασιν γάρ τινες δόλῳ πονηρῷ τὸ ὄνομα περιφέρειν, ἄλλα τινὰ πράσσοντες ἀνάξια θεοῦ: οὕς δεῖ ὑμᾶς ὡς θηρία ἐκκλίνειν: εἰσὶν γὰρ κύνες λυσσῶντες, λαθροδῆκται: οὓς δεῖ ὑμᾶς φυλάσσεσθαι ὄντας δυσθεραπεύτους. [2] εἷς ἰατρός ἐστιν, σαρκικός τε καὶ πνευματικός, γεννητὸς καὶ ἀγέννητος, ἐν ἀνθρώπῳ θεός, ἐν θανάτῳ ζωὴ ἀληθινή, καὶ ἐκ Μαρίας καὶ ἐκ θεοῦ, πρῶτον παθητὸς καὶ τότε ἀπαθής. Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν.
pass_a_gloss: For some are in the habit of carrying the Name around with wicked deceit, while doing other things unworthy of God. You must avoid them as wild beasts. For they are mad dogs that bite secretly; you must be on guard against them, since they are hard to cure. There is one physician, both of flesh and of spirit, begotten and unbegotten, God in man, true life in death, both from Mary and from God, first subject to suffering and then not subject to suffering: Jesus Christ our Lord.
pass_b_english: Some people make a habit of carrying the Name around with wicked cunning, while they do other things unworthy of God. Shun them as you would wild beasts. They are rabid dogs that bite by stealth. Be on guard against them, for they are hard to cure.
There is one Physician: flesh and spirit, born and unborn, God in man, true life in death, from Mary and from God, first able to suffer and then beyond suffering, Jesus Christ our Lord.

choices.why: Lake reads γεννητός/ἀγέννητος: born as man, unborn as God. Ignatius predates the later begotten/unbegotten Trinitarian vocabulary, so 'born and unborn' keeps his paradox plain.
rejected: made and not made (ANF; follows the γενητός spelling)

choices.why: Lake's text. Short, paradoxical, matches the rhythm of the list.
rejected: God existing in flesh (ANF; follows the variant ἐν σαρκὶ γενόμενος θεός)

choices.english: first able to suffer and then beyond suffering
choices.why: Plain words for passible/impassible: mortal suffering first, then risen life beyond it.
Capitalized as a title of Christ; answers δυσθεραπεύτους (hard to heal) just before.

anf_compare.notes: ANF translates a different text at two points: 'made and not made' reflects γενητὸς καὶ ἀγένητος, and 'God existing in flesh' reflects the variant ἐν σαρκὶ γενόμενος θεός. Lake prints γεννητὸς καὶ ἀγέννητος and ἐν ἀνθρώπῳ θεός, translated here. Rest aligned.

variants: γεννητὸς καὶ ἀγέννητος (Lake) vs γενητὸς καὶ ἀγένητος (behind ANF)
ἐν ἀνθρώπῳ θεός (Lake) vs ἐν σαρκὶ γενόμενος θεός (behind ANF; Athanasius and others)
notes: Whole chapter 7 (sections 1-2) matches the ANF span.
Possible echo: Philippians 3:2 ('beware of the dogs'); not close enough to cite inline.

Same chapter serves ignatius_eph_7_doctor and ignatius_eph_7_incarn; English kept identical. Consistent with existing ignatius_ephesians_7_physician except 'born and unborn' and 'God in man' (choices above).

review.notes: Paragraph 1 keeps both warnings and the physician paradox. Greek 'Εἰώθασιν γάρ τινες δόλῳ πονηρῷ τὸ ὄνομα περιφέρειν, ἄλλα τινὰ πράσσοντες ἀνάξια θεοῦ' matches A 'carrying the Name around with wicked deceit, while doing other things unworthy of God' and B 'carrying the Name around with wicked cunning, while they do other things unworthy of God'. 'οὕς δεῖ ὑμᾶς ὡς θηρία ἐκκλίνειν' and 'οὓς δεῖ ὑμᾶς φυλάσσεσθαι ὄντας δυσθεραπεύτους' remain in A 'must avoid them as wild beasts' / 'must be on guard against them, since they are hard to cure' and B 'Shun them as you would wild beasts' / 'Be on guard against them, for they are hard to cure'. The list 'σαρκικός τε καὶ πνευματικός, γεννητὸς καὶ ἀγέννητος, ἐν ἀνθρώπῳ θεός, ἐν θανάτῳ ζωὴ ἀληθινή, καὶ ἐκ Μαρίας καὶ ἐκ θεοῦ, πρῶτον παθητὸς καὶ τότε ἀπαθής. Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν' is kept: A 'begotten and unbegotten ... God in man ... first subject to suffering and then not subject to suffering: Jesus Christ our Lord'; B 'born and unborn ... God in man ... first able to suffer and then beyond suffering, Jesus Christ our Lord'. Alternate glosses do not flip negation, agency, or the first-then sequence. No scripture clause is quoted or miscited.

Source identity: Locked Greek is Ignatius Ephesians 7, matching Lake 1912 Loeb. Completeness: All clauses from both source paragraphs rendered in Pass A and B. Negation: No negation in source; none missed. Agency: Clear agency in 'some carry', 'you must avoid', 'there is one physician'. Modality: 'δεῖ' (must) properly rendered as 'must' in both passes. Doctrine: Christological terms 'born and unborn', 'God in man' preserved per choices. Scripture: No explicit biblical citations in source; bible_refs empty; no false or missing citations. Title 'Born and unborn, God in man' names the thought, not just locus. Pass A and B are faithful: no added or contradicted meaning. Covered source paragraphs: [1].
